deep.reconstruction:
Folio 107v contains no mathematics. It is an administrative document: a salary receipt (Quittung) written and signed by Riemann.

Content, normalized: 'Quittung über = 400 Thlr. Courant. Daß ich aus der Königlichen Universitäts-Casse zu Hannover [reading of the place name uncertain, see corrections] von dem mir gnädigst bewilligten [partly hidden under an ink blot] jährlichen Gehalt ad. 800 Thlr den Betrag auf das Semester von Michaelis 1859 bis Ostern 1860 mit = Vierhundert Th[aler] C[ourant] = durch den Herrn [title and name uncertain] richtig ausbezahlt erhalten habe, bescheinige ich hiedurch quittirend. Göttingen, am 8ten Januar 1860. B. Riemann, Professor.'

In English: Riemann confirms receiving 400 thaler Courant from the Royal University cash office. This is the half-year installment, Michaelmas 1859 to Easter 1860, of an annual salary of 800 thaler.

The only 'computation' is implicit: 800 / 2 = 400 per semester. That is correct.

Historical context: Riemann was appointed ordinary professor at Göttingen in summer 1859, succeeding Dirichlet. This is presumably among the first salary payments at his new rank, which is consistent with the title 'Professor' in the signature.

The red stain and the ink blot are physical damage. The sheet was evidently reused as scrap paper. The neighbouring folio 108 carries unrelated mathematics: the Fourier-integral solution of the 3D wave equation, reduced via spherical coordinates to Poisson's spherical-mean formula. That material belongs to the adjacent page, not this one.

results.what: Salary receipt: half-yearly installment of 400 Thaler of an 800 Thaler annual salary, Michaelmas 1859 to Easter 1860, dated Göttingen 8 January 1860, signed B. Riemann, Professor.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine salary receipt with no mathematical content. Its only interest is biographical: it confirms an 800-thaler annual salary shortly after Riemann's 1859 promotion, paid half-yearly. That is consistent with what is known of his career.

checkable.asserts: The semester installment of 400 Thaler is half of the annual salary of 800 Thaler.

transcription_corrections: The word partly hidden by the ink blot is almost certainly 'bewilligten' ('dem mir gnädigst bewilligten jährlichen Gehalt').
The currency line '= Vierhundert rh Ct. =' is more plausibly 'Vierhundert Th[ale]r C[ourant]', matching the heading '400 Thlr. Courant'; the reading remains uncertain.
Place of the cash office: the hand appears to read 'zu Hannover', but this is uncertain. 'zu Göttingen' cannot be excluded, given that the university treasury was locally in Göttingen.
The official's title and name ('Herrn Rentmeister Thiemann') are uncertain readings and should be checked against Göttingen university administration records of 1860.
